newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian debt finds upside tough going.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian debt finds upside tough going.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract is finding moves to the upside tough going, having failed to make a full recovery from last week's steep sell-off.
*The short end is also starting to wind back easing hopes.

The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract is finding moves to the upside tough going having failed to make a full recovery from last week's steep sell-off, ending SYCOM a fraction softer.
The contract ended the after-hours session at 93.380, down from Tuesday's 93.385 pit close, and having failed to break back above 93.410 resistance.

The bond has been consistently pegged on approaches to 93.470 since last week's U.S. inspired sell-off to 93.135, and a breach of support at 93.360 on the downside now could see at least a further five basis point sell-off, analysts said.

"It appears A$ bonds are set to fall. Spread watchers also note the A$ bonds undergoing a severe technical deterioration here and would turn away from compression trades vs NZD, CAD and US bonds," Peter Pontikis, technical strategist at Westpac Banking Corp, said in a report.

The short-end of the market also wound back some of its rate expectations in SYCOM, while the Australian dollar firmed as New York traders took to heart from an Australian Financial Review article that the Reserve Bank believed the economy was picking up and there would be no more rate cuts.
The article followed Tuesday's RBA quarterly bulletin.
However, local economists' reaction to the report were far less clear cut.

"(The RBA) report does not rule out another cut. Nor does it call for one either," said Annette Beacher, senior economist at Citibank Australia who is still giving a 30 percent chance of a further easing.
Meanwhile, the Federal Open Market Committee left U.S. monetary policy unchanged as widely expected, which saw the U.S. Treasury market end a fairly lacklustre session mixed.
